He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Boise State Broncos men's basketball|Boise State Broncos]].{{cite web|url=http://www.broncosports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/chandler_hutchison_914762.html|title=Chandler Hutchison|access-date=April 2, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180613134349/http://www.broncosports.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/chandler_hutchison_914762.html|archive-date=June 13, 2018|url-status=dead}} ==High school career== Hutchison lettered two years at [[Mission Viejo High School]]. As a junior, he averaged 13.8 points and 4.8 rebounds while leading Mission Viejo to the regional quarterfinals of the [[California Interscholastic Federation|CIF]] Southern Section 1AA Tournament. In his senior season, he was ranked No. 80 in the ESPN Top 100, the No. 7 prospect in California{{Cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/172531/chandler-hutchison|title=Chandler Hutchison – Basketball Recruiting – Player Profiles – ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=April 8, 2018}} and a consensus 4-star recruit by 247 Sports. He averaged 19.5 points and led Mission Viejo to the CIF Southern Section title game and regional quarterfinals of CIF State Championship tournament. ==College career== Hutchison posted 3.1 points per game as a freshman and started in the NCAA Tournament matchup versus [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]].{{cite news|last1=Walton|first1=Brandon|title=Boise State set to say farewell to Chandler Hutchison on Senior Night|url=https://www.idahopress.com/blueturfsports/basketball/boise-state-set-to-say-farewell-to-chandler-hutchison-on/article_117f361a-5914-591c-b45f-25b2dd2c9e2a.html|access-date=April 8, 2018|work=Idaho Press|date=March 2, 2018}} He averaged 6.8 points and 4.1 rebounds per game as a sophomore in 2015–16. With the departure of [[James Webb III]], coach [[Leon Rice]] began to look at Hutchison as more of an offensive threat, and he responded by hitting the weight room and remaking his jump shot. He had a breakout season as a junior, averaging 17.4 points, 7.8 rebounds and 2.6 assists per game while making 37.7% of his threes.{{cite news|last1=Fischer|first1=Jake|title=Chandler Hutchison is the NBA Draft's Hidden Gem|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2017/12/13/nba-draft-chandler-hutchison-boise-state-weber-state-damian-lillard|access-date=April 8, 2018|work=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=December 13, 2017}} He declared for the [[2017 NBA draft]] but returned to the Broncos. Hutchison had a stellar senior year, averaging 20 points and 7.7 rebounds per contest.{{cite news|last1=Roberts|first1=Rachel|title=From 'soft, immature, entitled' to the 'best player in Boise State history'|url=http://www.idahostatesman.com/sports/college/mountain-west/boise-state-university/boise-state-basketball/article199924644.html|access-date=April 8, 2018|work=[[Idaho Statesman]]|date=February 13, 2018}} As a senior, he was named to the First-team All-[[Mountain West Conference]].{{cite news|last1=Zeigler|first1=Mark|title=SDSU's Malik Pope named second team all-conference|url=http://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/sports/aztecs/sd-sp-sdsu-basketball-malik-pope-second-team-20180306-story.html|access-date=April 6, 2018|work=[[San Diego Union-Tribune]]|date=March 6, 2018}} Hutchison was a Top-10 Finalist for the [[Jerry West Award]] and a Top-30 Finalist for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year|Naismith Trophy]]. Hutchison also was one of two [[Mountain West Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|MW Players of the Year]], earning the honor from league media{{cite press release|url=https://themw.com/news/2018/3/19/mountain-west-mens-basketball-all-conference-media-awards.aspx |title=Mountain West Men's Basketball All-Conference Media Awards |publisher=Mountain West Conference |date=March 4, 2018 |access-date=October 20, 2018}} while [[2017–18 Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball team|Nevada's]] [[Caleb Martin (basketball)|Caleb Martin]] received the honor from the league's coaches.{{cite press release|url=https://themw.com/news/2018/3/6/mountain-west-announces-2017-18-mens-basketball-all-conference-team.aspx |title=Mountain West Announces 2017–18 Men's Basketball All-Conference Team |publisher=Mountain West Conference |date=March 6, 2018 |access-date=October 20, 2018}} ==Professional career== ===Chicago Bulls (2018–2021)=== Hutchison was drafted 22nd overall in the [[2018 NBA draft]] by the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite news|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/basketball/bulls/ct-spt-bulls-chandler-hutchison-draft-20180621-story.html|title=Bulls select Boise State's Chandler Hutchison with No. 22 pick in draft|newspaper=[[Chicago Tribune]]|last=Johnson|first=K.C.|date=June 21, 2018|access-date=June 21, 2018}} On July 3, 2018, Hutchison officially signed with the Bulls.{{cite web |date=July 3, 2018| title=Bulls sign Carter Jr. and Hutchison |url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-sign-carter-jr-and-hutchison |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 4, 2018 |language=en}} He made his NBA debut playing three minutes in a loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] on October 18.{{cite web |last1=Greenberg |first1=Daniel |title=Chicago Bulls: Chandler Hutchison played three minutes in his NBA debut |url=https://pippenainteasy.com/2018/10/19/chicago-bulls-chandler-hutchison-played-three-minutes-in-his-nba-debut/ |website=Pippen Ain't Easy |access-date=October 19, 2018 |date=October 19, 2018 |archive-date=January 9, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210109113936/https://pippenainteasy.com/2018/10/19/chicago-bulls-chandler-hutchison-played-three-minutes-in-his-nba-debut/ |url-status=dead }} On January 23, Hutchison suffered an acute injury to a sesamoid bone in his right foot.{{cite web|title=Chandler Hutchison Injury Update|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/chandler-hutchison-injury-update|date=January 26, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 26, 2019}} He was assigned to the Bulls’ [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Windy City Bulls]] to rehabilitate his injury on December 31, 2019.{{cite news|url= https://pippenainteasy.com/2019/12/31/chicago-bulls-chandler-hutchison-assigned-to-g-league-windy-city-bulls/|title= Chandler Hutchison assigned to G-League Windy City Bulls| website=Pippen Ain't Easy|last=Miller|first=Andrew|date=December 31, 2019|access-date=January 4, 2020}} ===Washington Wizards (2021)=== On March 25, 2021, Hutchison was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/wizards-acquire-gafford-and-hutchison|title=Wizards acquire Gafford and Hutchison|work=NBA.com|date=March 25, 2021}} On August 6, Hutchison was traded to the [[San Antonio Spurs]]{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/washington-acquires-six-players-five-team-trade|title=Washington acquires six players in five-team trade|work=NBA.com|date=August 6, 2021|access-date=August 6, 2021}} and was later waived on September 4.{{cite web |last1=Helin |first1=Kurt |title=Spurs waive wing Chandler Hutchinson, making him a free agent |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2021/09/05/spurs-waive-wing-chandler-hutchinson-making-him-a-free-agent/ |website=NBC Sports |access-date=September 6, 2021 |date=September 5, 2021}} ===Phoenix Suns (2021–2022)=== On September 7, 2021, Hutchison signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{cite web|title=Suns Sign Chandler Hutchison|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/suns-sign-chandler-hutchison|date=September 7, 2021|website=NBA.com|accessdate=September 7, 2021}} He played six games for the Suns, totaling 23 minutes. On January 4, 2022, he was waived.{{cite web |last1=Olson |first1=Kellan |title=Phoenix Suns waive 2-way forward Chandler Hutchison |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/2956047/phoenix-suns-waive-2-way-forward-chandler-hutchison/ |website=Arizona Sports |access-date=January 5, 2022 |date=January 4, 2022}} ===Sioux Falls Skyforce (2022)=== On February 1, 2022, Hutchison was acquired by the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]].{{cite web |title=SKYFORCE ACQUIRES CHANDLER HUTCHISON |url=https://siouxfalls.gleague.nba.com/news/skyforce-acquires-chandler-hutchison/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 1, 2022 |date=February 1, 2022}} Hutchison joined the [[Atlanta Hawks]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612737/hawks |access-date=July 5, 2022 |website=NBA.com}} He rejoined the Skyforce for the beginning of the [[2022–23 NBA G League season|2022–23 season]]. On November 29, 2022, Hutchison retired at the age of 26.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/chandler-hutchison-retires-at-age-26/#:~:text=Hutchison%20retired%20Wednesday%2C%20Ira%20Winderman,NBA%20Draft%20by%20the%20Bulls.|website=cbssports.com|title= Chandler Hutchison: Retires at age 26|access-date=November 30, 2022|date=November 30, 2022}} However on October 25, 2024, he came out of retirement to enter the 2024 NBA G League draft.{{cite web|title=Former NBA 1st-Round Pick Reportedly Coming Out Of Retirement|url=https://www.si.com/fannation/nba/fastbreak/former-nba-1st-round-pick-reportedly-coming-out-of-retirement-chandler-hutchison|website=SI.com|date=October 25, 2024|access-date=October 25, 2024}} ===Cleveland Charge (2024–present)=== On October 26, 2024, Hutchison joined the [[Cleveland Charge]].{{cite web|title=Cleveland Charge 2024 Training Camp Roster|url=https://cleveland.gleague.nba.com/news/cleveland-charge-2024-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 26, 2024|access-date=October 26, 2024}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player
